confidenceNote: This is a temperament read, not a measurement. It picks the lever you REACH FOR, which is a real and useful thing to know about yourself — but it is not where your money actually moves. That comes later, from your numbers, and the two disagreeing is the interesting part rather than an error.
note: Five questions, no maths, no jargon, and no answer that makes you look daft. Each option leans on one or more of the seven class levers; the highest total wins and the runner-up is shown, because almost nobody is one pure thing.

questions.ask: A thousand pounds just landed in your account. Nobody wants it back.
questions.sub: Be honest. Not what you'd tell your accountant.

options.label: Straight into savings. I sleep better knowing it's sat there.
options.says: You buy calm before you buy upside. That is a whole strategy, not a lack of one.

options.label: Into the investments, with everything else.
options.says: You'd rather your money did the work. You are playing a long game on purpose.

options.label: That's the seed money for the thing I keep meaning to start.
options.says: You back yourself over the market. Expensive when it's wrong, enormous when it isn't.

options.label: I've got a punt in mind. Small odds, silly number.
options.says: You're comfortable being wrong most of the time for one very good day.

options.label: Onto the card. It's been annoying me for months.
options.says: You clear the noise first. Unglamorous and almost always correct.

questions.ask: Your boss says there's room for exactly one thing this year.

options.label: More money. Obviously more money.
options.says: You go at the number directly. The most reliable lever there is, and the least used.

options.label: A better title. The money follows the title.
options.says: You play two moves ahead. Slower this year, larger by the third.

options.label: Fully remote. Permanently, in writing.
options.says: You're buying the ability to leave. That is worth more than most raises.

options.label: Training in something I could sell on my own later.
options.says: You're using their budget to build your exit. Cheeky, and correct.

questions.ask: Sunday, eight in the evening. A free hour and a faint nagging feeling about money.
questions.sub: What do you actually end up doing?

options.label: Going through every subscription and cancelling with real menace.
options.says: You find money by removing things. It compounds quietly and nobody claps.

options.label: Reading about something I might buy into.
options.says: You enjoy the machinery. That curiosity is worth actual money over thirty years.

options.label: Looking at what places near me went for.
options.says: You think in bricks. Slow, lumpy, and it has made more ordinary people wealthy than anything else.

options.label: Quietly updating my CV. No reason.
options.says: You keep an exit warm. People who do this get paid more, mostly by leaving.

options.label: Checking the balance, feeling broadly fine, closing the app.
options.says: Nothing wrong with this. It is only a problem if the feeling is doing the checking for you.

questions.ask: A mate has a thing. He describes it as can't-lose.
questions.sub: Your first thought, before politeness kicks in.

options.label: How much can I lose, and could I take it?
options.says: You size the hole before the prize. This is the single best habit on this page.

options.label: What's the actual return once everything's paid?
options.says: You go straight past the story to the arithmetic. Good. The story is the sales pitch.

options.label: Nothing is can't-lose. I'm out.
options.says: You'll miss a few good ones. You'll also still be here in ten years, which is the game.

options.label: In. Life's short and he's usually right.
options.says: You move fast. Make sure the amount is one you can genuinely shrug at.

options.label: Could I just do that myself, without him?
options.says: You see a business where others see an offer. That instinct is rare and it pays.

questions.ask: Which of these would genuinely ruin your month?
questions.sub: Last one. Then we'll tell you what you are.

options.label: Losing the job tomorrow morning.
options.says: Your instinct is to want a floor under you. Everything else is easier once it's there.

options.label: The market falling a third in the year I needed the money.
options.says: You already think in timing, not just returns. Most people learn that the hard way.

options.label: Being stuck — a city, a lease, a role I can't get out of.
options.says: You price freedom highly. Keep your fixed costs low and you'll always have it.

options.label: Finding out I've been quietly overpaying for years.
options.says: Waste offends you more than risk does. That is a genuinely useful thing to be.
